clippings.speaker: Lauren Bacall
clippings.quote: he changed me. He was my teacher, my husband, my friend. In his life and his work, Bogie was integrity, truth and courage. He taught me how to live. That it was okay to trust. He taught me how to keep going no matter what.
clippings.title: Bacall on Bogart
clippings.context: TCM article quoting Bacall in the 1988 PBS Great Performances documentary Bacall on Bogart.

clippings.speaker: Lauren Bacall
clippings.quote: Off screen he bore little resemblance to the parts he played. He was a gent.
clippings.title: Bacall on Bogart
clippings.context: From the 1988 documentary Bacall on Bogart, as quoted by TCM, on the difference between his screen persona and the man she married.

clippings.speaker: Lauren Bacall
clippings.quote: I never imagined I would meet anyone like Bogie and marry him and have children. And obviously, the minute I fell in love with him that's all I wanted. Then, of course, after we were married I wanted more. But I was a kid. I was 19 when I met him…
clippings.title: Remembering Lauren Bacall
clippings.context: From Brad Goldfarb's April 2004 Interview Q&A, reprinted in the magazine's 2014 tribute.

clippings.speaker: Lauren Bacall
clippings.quote: I married a man who was exactly the same. If anyone asked Bogie about whether he thought a movie was good or not, regardless of whether he was in it, he'd answer honestly. He could not lie, and I'm the same.
clippings.title: Remembering Lauren Bacall
clippings.context: From the 2004 Interview Q&A reprinted in 2014, on speaking her mind in Hollywood.

clippings.speaker: Lauren Bacall
clippings.quote: Had I not met Bogie and then met all of his friends — his contemporaries — I never would've known Robert Benchley, Dorothy Parker, Louis Bromfield, all the journalists, sports figures, it's truly amazing.
clippings.title: Lauren Bacall Talks Favorite Hollywood Memories & Career in Unpublished Interview
clippings.context: Previously unpublished excerpts from a 1996 interview promoting The Mirror Has Two Faces.

clippings.speaker: Humphrey Bogart
clippings.quote: Do you realize what you do? You're a wife, a mother, an actress, you're running a house … that's a lot!
clippings.title: Lauren Bacall Talks Favorite Hollywood Memories & Career in Unpublished Interview
clippings.context: Bacall recalling, in a 1996 interview, what Bogart once said to her.

clippings.speaker: Humphrey Bogart
clippings.quote: I wish I were your age again – perhaps a few years older – and no ties of any kind – no responsibilities – it would be so lovely, for there would be so many long years ahead for us instead of the few possible ones.
clippings.title: Married at Malabar: The “Reel” Romance of Humphrey Bogart and Lauren Bacall
clippings.context: From a June 1944 letter Bogart wrote to Bacall while still married to Mayo Methot, quoted in a Mansfield/Richland County library blog post.

clippings.speaker: Humphrey Bogart
clippings.quote: Sure, Baby [his nickname for Bacall] and I are engaged. I know I open my fat yap too much and maybe this announcement is a little premature. But what the hell?
clippings.title: Married at Malabar: The “Reel” Romance of Humphrey Bogart and Lauren Bacall
clippings.context: Bogart to reporter Inez Robb in January 1945, as quoted in the library blog's history of the Malabar Farm wedding.

notes: Bogart direction is all secondhand (letters and press remarks relayed by Bacall or later writers); no open contemporaneous Bogart interview found. Parade (403) and Hollywood Reporter (paywall redirect) skipped.
